title: COMP 4537 · Midterm
subtitle: Exam week Oct 26–30: two hours on the Learning Hub, one double-sided letter cheat sheet; lectures 1 to 6 in full and the Node-to-MySQL part of lecture 7
description: The midterm in its own four question kinds. The rules and scope with a strategy for each kind; twenty new what-prints programs on timers, scope, hoisting, promises, chaining and async/await, each run in the browser after you commit to an answer; a short-answer bank (REST's constraints, GET vs POST, CORS and preflight, blocking vs non-blocking, localStorage vs sessionStorage, idempotency, readyState, monolith vs microservices, the four XHR steps, PHP's four steps vs Node's three) with key points to tick; coding questions (a Node server that returns the date in blue, an XHR GET, a callback rewritten as a promise chain, CORS headers, a query string); two forty-item mock midterms in the exam's mix; the cheat sheet as a lesson and a print-ready letter page; and a closed-book recall drill of every fixed list in the course.
intro:
:::quiz Midterm facts
**Exam week Oct 26–30 2026; check the Learning Hub for your day.** In person, on the Learning Hub on your own laptop, at most **two hours**, worth **30 % of the course**. One browser tab only; no developer tools. Closed book except **one letter-sized sheet, both sides, written or typed, figures allowed, your name top-left**; it may be collected. Scope: lectures 1 to 6 in full; lecture 7 only the Node.js database connection, sending queries from Node, and CRUD fundamentals. No complicated SQL, no hosting or deployment tools, no VS Code. Four kinds of question: multiple choice, coding, short answers, medium and long answers. Lecture 6 (promises) is the heaviest single topic.
:::

steps.note: the rules, the scope, and how to attack each question kind (5 min)
take it cold and timed, about 100 minutes, no notes
write every output before you run it; redo each one you missed
answer in writing, then tick the key points honestly
write the Node server, the XHR call and the promise chain from a blank editor
print the sheet; add in pen what you still missed
the second paper; aim for 80 % or better
